h: Bison, Reculver and the Blean Woods
p: Wildwood Trust has been at the heart of some exciting conservation projects in Kent. One of the most talked-about is the Wilder Blean project, a partnership with Kent Wildlife Trust that brought European bison back to the woods of West Blean in 2022, the first time wild bison had roamed in Britain for thousands of years. They help to manage the woodland naturally by stripping bark and creating clearings, which benefits other wildlife.

That story is a cracking talking point for kids as they walk past the wolves and lynx: which animals could come back, and which ones probably never should? It turns a nice walk into a proper debate. Give yourself time, too, as the quieter animals often only show themselves to the people who wait a minute longer at the fence.

Nearby, the Blean Woods offer plenty of walking trails for families to explore. If you're interested in history, Reculver Towers, a few miles east of Herne Bay, is a striking landmark with the remains of a Roman fort and the twin towers of a medieval church perched on the coast. It's a great spot for a picnic with sea views.
Herne Bay's seafront is also worth a stroll, with its clock tower, bandstand and gardens, plus plenty of spots for an ice cream or fish and chips.

Inland, the village of Herne has a fine old smock windmill on the edge of the village that opens to visitors on selected days, a quirky little extra if you're passing. Back on the seafront, look out to sea from Herne Bay's pier and you'll spot the old pier head standing alone in the water. The Victorian pier once stretched a very long way out until storms in 1978 wrecked the middle section, leaving the end stranded out at sea, where it's become a much-loved local landmark.
